name: Calf raise
angleNote: Plantarflexion: 0° = foot flat (at right angles to the shin), negative = heel below the step (stretch), 40° = up on the toes. Knee at the origin.

segments.note: Knee→ankle, and ankle→ball of the foot (0.161 m: 14 cm in front of and 8 cm below the ankle joint) in metres. Closed chain: the floor carries the foot's own weight, so no limb weight is added.

strengthCurve.label: Plantarflexor strength
strengthCurve.note: Relative isometric plantarflexion torque vs plantarflexion (negative = dorsiflexed), peak about 23° of dorsiflexion, measured with the knee bent 50° (tested 29° dorsiflexion to 34° plantarflexion). Relative curve = cos(C2·(θ − C3)) with the 18–25-year-old male means of Table 3; points only inside the tested range, so the app holds the end values flat beyond it. Peak torque default from the same table's C1 (young men, scaled to 73 kg and 1.75 m). Measured with the knee bent, where the gastrocnemius is slack. Peak default: Anderson's knee-bent mean (119 Nm). The variants then correct it for the knee angle with Cresswell et al.'s measurements (×1.20 standing, knee straight: 143 Nm, close to Lategan's 131 Nm and Cresswell's own 135 Nm with the knee straight).
strengthCurve.source: Anderson DE, Madigan ML, Nussbaum MA (2007). Maximum voluntary joint torque as a function of joint angle and angular velocity: model development and application to the lower limb. J Biomech 40(14):3105–3113. doi:10.1016/j.jbiomech.2007.03.022; cross-checks: Cresswell AG, Löscher WN, Thorstensson A (1995). Exp Brain Res 105:283–290 (Table 1); Lategan L (2002). Normative isokinetic torque values for rehabilitation in South Africa. DPhil thesis, University of Pretoria (Table 6.5)

muscles.name: Gastrocnemius
muscles.note: Crosses the knee too: with the knee bent (seated) it is slack and contributes much less.
muscles.source: Weights: TODO. Knee-angle effect: Baptista MT, Nascimento FXM, Nardes LK, Matta TT, Oliveira LF (2014). Influência de posições do joelho no torque e atividade mioelétrica do tríceps sural na flexão plantar isométrica máxima. Rev Bras Educ Fís Esporte 28(2):197–202. doi:10.1590/1807-55092014000200197; Kovács B, Csala D, Yang S, Tihanyi J, Gu Y, Hortobágyi T (2024). Knee position affects medial gastrocnemius and soleus activation during dynamic plantarflexion: no evidence for an inter-muscle compensation in healthy young adults. Biol Open 13:bio061810. doi:10.1242/bio.061810

muscles.name: Soleus
muscles.note: Crosses the ankle only, so it works whatever the knee angle.

phases.name: Stretch
phases.text: Heel below the step: the ball of the foot is furthest in front of the ankle, so the moment arm is largest.

phases.name: Mid-range
phases.text: Rising onto the toes turns the ankle→ball lever more vertical, so its horizontal reach (the moment arm) shrinks.

phases.name: Top
phases.text: High on the toes: smaller moment arm, but the calves are weakest here too.

variants.name: Single-leg standing calf raise (dumbbell)
variants.notes: Closed chain: the floor pushes up on the ball of the foot with your whole body weight plus the dumbbell. Torque = (body + m)·g × the horizontal distance from the ankle to the ball of the foot.

strengthScale.note: knee straight, so the gastrocnemius is at a useful length. At and below foot-flat, about 120% of the base curve's (measured with the knee bent 50°): Cresswell et al. measured 134.9 Nm with the knee straight vs about 112 Nm at 50° (interpolated between their 30° and 60°); Baptista et al. and Kovács et al. found 28–31% less torque at 90° of knee bend than straight. Towards the top of the raise the gap grows, because the knee-bent curve falls to 21% of its foot-flat value at 34° of plantarflexion. Above foot flat the factor follows the OpenSim leg model's knee-straight curve (its plantarflexors' force × moment arm with force–length), anchored to Cresswell's 1.2 at foot flat: the knee-straight curve keeps 74% of its foot-flat value at 20° and 45% at 34° (the base curve's last measured angle), in line with the datasets Chen & Franklin collected with the knee extended (about 70% at 20°, about half at 30°, individual datasets 30–70%). Below foot flat the model gives less (0.88 at 20° of dorsiflexion); the measured 1.2 is kept there.
strengthScale.source: Cresswell AG, Löscher WN, Thorstensson A (1995). Influence of gastrocnemius muscle length on triceps surae torque development and electromyographic activity in man. Exp Brain Res 105:283–290 (Table 1: 10 men, isometric, ankle 5° dorsiflexed); Baptista MT, Nascimento FXM, Nardes LK, Matta TT, Oliveira LF (2014). Influência de posições do joelho no torque e atividade mioelétrica do tríceps sural na flexão plantar isométrica máxima. Rev Bras Educ Fís Esporte 28(2):197–202. doi:10.1590/1807-55092014000200197; Kovács B, Csala D, Yang S, Tihanyi J, Gu Y, Hortobágyi T (2024). Knee position affects medial gastrocnemius and soleus activation during dynamic plantarflexion: no evidence for an inter-muscle compensation in healthy young adults. Biol Open 13:bio061810. doi:10.1242/bio.061810; Chen Z, Franklin DW (2025). Joint moment–angle/velocity relations in the hip, knee, and ankle: a meta-visualization of datasets. J Biomech 183 (bioRxiv preprint, CC BY 4.0: Fig. 11, bottom left, ankle moments with the knee extended or slightly flexed, read off the figure); above foot flat: Rajagopal AS, Dembia CL, DeMers MS, Delp DD, Hicks JL, Delp SL (2016). Full-body musculoskeletal model for muscle-driven simulation of human gait. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 63(10):2068–2079 (Rajagopal2016.osim, OpenSim 4.6: plantarflexor force × moment arm with force–length, knee straight, via tools/opensim_export.py)

variants.name: Standing calf raise machine (two legs)
variants.notes: Each leg carries half your body weight plus half the load (the load slider is per leg).

variants.name: Seated calf raise machine
variants.notes: The load sits on the knees, so body weight isn't lifted. With the knee bent the gastrocnemius is slack: its EMG fell by about a third (Baptista et al.: −41% lateral, −32% medial head; Kovács et al.: −35% medial head), hence the 0.65 factor. The soleus results differ between studies (more active in Baptista et al., unchanged in Cresswell et al.), so it keeps its weight.

strengthScale.note: knee bent 90°, gastrocnemius slack: about 92% of the base curve's strength (Cresswell et al.: 103.7 Nm at 90° vs about 112 Nm at 50°).
strengthScale.source: Cresswell AG, Löscher WN, Thorstensson A (1995). Influence of gastrocnemius muscle length on triceps surae torque development and electromyographic activity in man. Exp Brain Res 105:283–290 (Table 1: 10 men, isometric, ankle 5° dorsiflexed)
